Subject: Performance MAP: test plan, access, and load windows

Hi Anna / DataCo ops team,

Thanks again for agreeing to include Redwood in your MAP. Attached is an initial performance MAP and test plan (RW_MAP_PerfPlan_v1.xlsx) that outlines the evaluation metrics we discussed and proposed logistics. High level asks are below — can you confirm?

- Goals: validate candidate service at target throughput for pilot (10k RPS burst -> target sustained 6k RPS across 30m window), concurrency up to 128 virtual clients, and TTFT/latency SLOs (median TTFT < 700ms, p95 latency < 1.5s for 16-token responses).
- Required access: dedicated test API key(s) with throttling disabled for test CID RW-12458, sandbox service endpoint (URL and region), and one test account with sample payloads.
- Test artifacts: we will run the attached k6/locust scripts (load-scripts.tar.gz) from two geographic runners (us-west and us-east). Scripts will exercise prompt templates in sheet 'Workloads'.
- Windows: proposed windows (please pick one): Oct 1 09:00-11:00 PDT (preferred), Oct 2 06:00-08:00 PDT (backup). Each run: ramp 10m, steady 30m, cool-down 5m.
- Reporting: we will upload raw traces to the shared drive and provide a results summary in the MAP sheet. Quick wins we expect to capture: p50/p95 latency, TTFT distribution, token/sec, and KV cache hit rate.

Please reply with: (1) which window you can support, (2) the test key+endpoint, and (3) any onboarding steps for Helios/Cloud runners. If you'd like a short sync to finalize runbook, we can do a 15-min call tomorrow.

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Exec | Redwood Inference

Two asks from our side: please include a short canary plan (3-minute smoke at 500 RPS) before the main window and a rollback checklist in the runbook. Also confirm the exact payload sizes and prompts you will use (sheet 'Workloads').

I'll send the credential email shortly and upload a minimal runbook stub to your Drive link.

Sergio / Laura / Karthik,

We completed the planned run this morning and uploaded the run artifacts and initial summary to the Drive link (folder: RW-2026-12458/PerfRuns/2026-10-01). High level findings below — full numbers and raw traces are in the sheet 'Results'.

- Run configuration: steady target 6k RPS (2 runners), concurrency cap 128 virtual clients, median request size ~120 tokens.
- Throughput: sustained average 5.8k RPS during steady window (10% jitter).
- Latency: TTFT median 740ms, p95 1.34s for 120-token responses. P50 latency reported ~320ms (server-side).
- Concurrency/Utilization: average GPU utilization 72%, peak 88% during ramp. Token/sec peaked at ~95k tokens/sec aggregate.
- Observations: KV cache hit-rate ~18% (lower than expected with our prefix caching); a single instance showed a tail-drop event at minute 18 correlated with a batch scheduling delay — we've captured the trace.

Action items we propose:
1) Redwood to try a follow-up run with cache warming (5-min warmup at 1k RPS) to measure impact on hit rate.
2) We'll share the trace for the tail event; Redwood and DataCo can sync to root-cause and determine if model variant fallback occurred.

Overall: the service met the core throughput target (within 3%); TTFT is slightly above the target of <700ms for this payload mix. The attached MAP sheet includes an updated "status" column for each MAP milestone.

Thanks — the artifacts are in Drive and I've linked the dashboard snapshot.

—Anna
